verdict: Mettler Toledo's sales rose 6% to $1.1B — Asia grew 16% — and profit rose 13% to $246M as demand for its precision instruments firmed up.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: +16% YoY — few shares, high price per share

segments.name: Precision instruments & services
segments.note: Laboratory balances and pipettes, industrial weighing, product-inspection systems and supermarket scales, plus services. Mettler reports as one business; by region, sales rose 3% in the Americas, were flat in Europe and rose 16% in Asia/Rest of World.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: A direct sales and service force in dozens of countries — Mettler's distribution model is its moat.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $16M, partly offset by $6M of other income, net.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Asia is pulling the growth
takeaways.text: Sales rose 16% in Asia/Rest of World versus 3% in the Americas and flat Europe — demand for lab and industrial instruments is recovering fastest outside the West.

takeaways.title: Pricing power in precision
takeaways.text: Gross margin widened to 59.8% — customers pay up for instruments that labs and factories depend on for accuracy, and Mettler's service army keeps them loyal.

takeaways.title: Big EPS, tiny share count
takeaways.text: EPS rose 16% — faster than the 13% profit growth — because decades of buybacks have shrunk the share count to about 20 million.

footerNote: Figures are rounded to $M from the release's thousands presentation. Mettler's adjusted operating profit was $333.5M, excluding restructuring and the other items it adjusts for; the chart follows its GAAP statement, in which interest expense sits below gross profit alongside the operating lines.
